newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak constructor attacks Hungary dam claims.
newsitem.headline: Slovak constructor attacks Hungary dam claims.

text.p: A senior Slovak official accused neighbouring Hungary of conducting a propaganda campaign ahead of an international court hearing over a controversial dam project.

The International Court of Justice in The Hague is due to start hearings next Monday over Slovakia's unilateral decision to take water from the Danube River for the project in 1992 after Hungary quit an agreement that envisaged a similar dam on its side of the border.
"The experts know that the Hungarian side cannot win," Julius Binder, director of Gabcikovo dam's general constructor Vodohospodarska Vystavba s.p., said.

Binder, who has been strongly supported by Slovakia's nationalist government and is considered the "father of Gabcikovo", accused Hungary of carrying out an inappropriate campaign over the suit before the public hearings at the court start next Monday.
"There is propaganda of an international soccer match type from the Hungarian side... which is undignified for the court in The Hague," he said.
"But if somebody wants to speak in soccer terms, then I say Slovakia will win, at worst, eight to two."
The court is expected to announce its final ruling on the case in the autumn. Both countries officially presented their cases in 1993.

Slovakia says Hungary was the first to breach a contract, originally signed in 1977 by communist leaders of both countries, while the Hungarian side says a diversion of the Danube broke international law.
